subject: [PATCH v2 1/2] mm: refactor find_next_best_node to find_next_best_node_in

2026-09-12.patch_summary: This patch refactors the find_next_best_node function to find_next_best_node_in, which takes an explicit candidates nodemask instead of relying on N_MEMORY. This change enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates without changing any existing functionality. The new function is used in memory-tiers.c and page_alloc.c, where it replaces calls to the original function. The patch includes changes to internal.h, memory-tiers.c, and page_alloc.c, adding a new function signature and updating callers accordingly.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Identified the patch as LGTM and provided Reviewed-by tag without any technical discussion or concerns.
reviews.raw_body:
On 11 Sep 2026, at 23:04, Gregory Price wrote:

> find_next_best_node() picks the next-closest node for a fallback list
> from the full N_MEMORY set. Refactor it into find_next_best_node_in(),
> which takes an explicit candidates nodemask.
>
> This enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates.
>
> No functional change: every caller still selects from N_MEMORY.
>
> Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
> Acked-by: Balbir Singh <balbirs@nvidia.com>
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price <gourry@gourry.net>

Yan, Zi

2026-09-14.patch_summary: The patch refactors the find_next_best_node() function to take an explicit candidates nodemask, enabling fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY nodes. The existing callers still select from N_MEMORY, but this change allows for more flexibility in building fallback lists.
